items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I started Juggernaut with Nat Pierce

ctx.x: Did this kind of popularity kind of come overnight for you?

Well actually, I’ve kind of been, over the last many years I’ve been kind of hidden as it were, by studio work. But back in 1976 I decided that I had enough of that, you know I mean not that I still don’t do an occasional studio call, but that was my main focus after I got off the road with the bands, the many bands I played with and acts and all of that, I settled in at the studios. And I made a good living doing that. And never gave up, ever gave up playing jazz. But unfortunately studio musicians don’t get any…
You are East Coast — moved to the West Coast.
